title: Made-Good Relief on Credit Builder Accounts by Kind of Returned Payment
content:
The made-good relief on a Credit Builder account depends on what kind of payment the most recent returned payment was and, for an AutoPay debit, on how quickly it was made good. The rule acts on the amount the relief share gives on the returned-payment fee, and the relief is rounded to the cent after it.

## Kind of payment returned

- When that returned payment was an AutoPay debit (the payment its return line points at was made through the AutoPay channel), the relief is reduced by one sixtieth for each calendar day after the return date up to and including the date of the payment that made it good, and never below zero.
- When the returned payment was any other payment for less than the monthly payment, the relief is halved (multiplied by 0.5).
- When the returned payment was any other payment for the monthly payment or more, the relief keeps its full amount.

The payment that made it good is the latest payment posted toward the due date the returned payment was meant to pay, dated after the return date. In the AutoPay case the relief is multiplied by 1 less the number of days divided by 60, and is zero from 60 days on.

| Returned payment | Made good | Relief |
|---|---|---|
| AutoPay debit | 1 day after the return | 59 sixtieths |
| AutoPay debit | 15 days after the return | 45 sixtieths |
| AutoPay debit | 60 or more days after the return | zero |
| other payment, below the monthly payment | any | halved |
| other payment, the monthly payment or more | any | full |

## Worked figures (hypothetical)

The relief share gives 4.00 on the fee. An AutoPay debit returned on 3 October and made good by a payment dated 18 October: 15 days, 4.00 times 45 divided by 60, that is 3.00. A one-time payment of 25.00 returned on a plan with a monthly payment of 100.00: 2.00.
